questions.topic: Journalism — perspectives, rhetoric and opinion writing
questions.prompt: OPINION ARTICLE PRACTICE — Write 180–250 words responding to: “Every student should have one homework-free evening each week.” Build a clear viewpoint and address one counterargument.

markPoints: clear controlling viewpoint
engaging opening
at least two persuasive or rhetorical methods used purposefully
acknowledgement and response to a counterargument
coherent structure with a purposeful ending or call to action
answer.modelAnswer: A strong response would establish a clear position immediately, use one concrete example or anecdote, develop two reasons, acknowledge a reasonable objection about lost study time, rebut it by focusing on purposeful scheduling, and finish with a concise recommendation rather than repeating the introduction.

feedback.short: Suggested answer: A strong response would establish a clear position immediately, use one concrete example or anecdote, develop two reasons, acknowledge a reasonable objection about lost study time, rebut it by focusing on purposeful scheduling, and finish with a concise recommendation rather than repeating the introduction.
steps: Use the task requirements as a checklist before writing.
Criterion 1: clear controlling viewpoint.
Criterion 2: engaging opening.
Criterion 3: at least two persuasive or rhetorical methods used purposefully.
Criterion 4: acknowledgement and response to a counterargument.
Criterion 5: coherent structure with a purposeful ending or call to action.
feedback.commonError: Writing fluently but missing one or more explicit task requirements.
feedback.remember: Success checklist: clear controlling viewpoint; engaging opening; at least two persuasive or rhetorical methods used purposefully; acknowledgement and response to a counterargument; coherent structure with a purposeful ending or call to action.

note.title: Journalism — perspectives, rhetoric and opinion writing
note.overview: Analyse journalistic viewpoint and construct a persuasive, coherent opinion article.
mustMemoriseRules: A persuasive device is only useful if you explain what it is doing.
Comparison should move between writers around the same idea.
A strong opinion piece anticipates a reader rather than merely announcing an opinion.
workedExamples: A contrast in verbs can reveal how two writers frame the same event differently.
A counterargument can strengthen persuasion when it is represented fairly and answered thoughtfully.
commonMistakes: Listing persuasive devices without connecting them to viewpoint.
Writing two separate summaries instead of a comparison.
Using exaggerated claims without evidence or qualification.
detailedExplanation: The curriculum scope and assessed skills are verified against the official Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 English Curriculum Outline 2026-27.
Practice articles, extracts and poem-like lines in this bank are newly written for the app and are not copies of the school’s assessment materials.
Long article, poem and presentation responses are practice/self-check tasks and do not by themselves create formal Mastery evidence.
examTips: Explain how structure changes emphasis or audience response.
Use terminology accurately but keep the interpretation central.
Compare writers through ideas and methods, not two separate mini-essays.
beforeStartingPractice: Recall the core methods and command words before beginning.
